ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Anyone who's had an apple may know that pieces of an apple stick together, when picking up one piece a second piece may also come with the first piece. The same idea is tried on a golden apple. Consider two uniform hemispheres with radius $r=4 \mathrm{~cm}$ made of gold of density $\rho_{g}=19300 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$. The top half is nailed to a support and the space between is filled with water.
<image_1>

Given that the surface tension of water is $\gamma=0.072 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$ and that the contact angle between gold and water is $\theta=10^{\circ}$, what is the maximum distance between the two hemispheres so that the bottom half doesn't fall? Answer in millimeters.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper gold hemisphere is fixed to the upper support plate through a small nail or rod; the lower hemisphere is located directly below it. There is a very thin horizontal water layer between the planar circular cross-sections of the two hemispheres, and a meniscus forms at the edge, indicating that water fills the approximately parallel narrow gap and supports the lower hemisphere through capillary action. According to the specified method, use the parallel-plate narrow-gap approximation. The capillary pressure difference of water is Delta p ≈ 2 gamma cos(theta) / d. This pressure acts on the circular cross-sectional area A = pi r^2, giving the lower hemisphere an upward supporting force F = Delta p pi r^2. The weight of the lower hemisphere is W = rho_g g V = rho_g g (2/3 pi r^3). At the critical condition of not falling, set the two equal: (2 gamma cos(theta) / d) pi r^2 = rho_g g (2/3 pi r^3). After canceling common factors, obtain d = 3 gamma cos(theta) / (rho_g g r). Substituting r = 0.04 m, rho_g = 19300 kg/m^3, gamma = 0.072 N/m, theta = 10°, g = 9.81 m/s^2: d = 3(0.072)cos(10°)/(19300*9.81*0.04) m ≈ 2.81e-5 m. Converting to millimeters: 2.81e-5 m = 0.0281 mm.

raw_record.question_text:
Anyone who's had an apple may know that pieces of an apple stick together: when picking up one piece, a second piece may also come with the first piece. The same idea is tried on a golden apple. Consider two uniform hemispheres with radius $r=4\ \mathrm{cm}$ made of gold of density $\rho_g=19300\ \mathrm{kg\ m^{-3}}$. The top half is nailed to a support and the space between them is filled with water.

Given that the surface tension of water is $\gamma=0.072\ \mathrm{N\ m^{-1}}$ and that the contact angle between gold and water is $\theta=10^{\circ}$, what is the maximum distance between the two hemispheres so that the bottom half doesn't fall? Answer in millimeters.

method.method_draft: Use a direct capillary-pressure force balance. From the image, identify that the water occupies a thin, nearly parallel gap between the flat circular faces of two hemispheres, with the bottom hemisphere supported only by the water meniscus. From the text, take r = 4 cm, gold density rho_g = 19300 kg/m^3, surface tension gamma = 0.072 N/m, and contact angle theta = 10 degrees. Treat the gap distance d as small compared with r, so the meniscus is approximated as that between parallel plates. Use the Young-Laplace pressure drop for a wetting liquid in a narrow gap: Delta p approximately 2 gamma cos(theta) / d. The upward holding force is Delta p times the circular area pi r^2. Set this equal to the weight of the lower gold hemisphere, rho_g g (2/3 pi r^3), and solve for d: d = 3 gamma cos(theta)/(rho_g g r). Convert the result from meters to millimeters.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上半个金质半球通过一个小钉或杆固定在上方支撑板上；下半个半球位于其正下方。两个半球的平面圆形截面之间有一层很薄的水平水层，边缘处形成弯月面，说明水填充在近似平行的窄缝中，并通过毛细作用支撑下半球。

按指定方法，用平行板窄缝近似。水的毛细压强差为 Delta p ≈ 2 gamma cos(theta) / d。该压强作用在圆形截面积 A = pi r^2 上，给下半球的向上托举力 F = Delta p pi r^2。下半球重量为 W = rho_g g V = rho_g g (2/3 pi r^3)。临界不下落时令二者相等：
(2 gamma cos(theta) / d) pi r^2 = rho_g g (2/3 pi r^3)。
约去公共因子后得到 d = 3 gamma cos(theta) / (rho_g g r)。
代入 r = 0.04 m, rho_g = 19300 kg/m^3, gamma = 0.072 N/m, theta = 10°, g = 9.81 m/s^2：
d = 3(0.072)cos(10°)/(19300*9.81*0.04) m ≈ 2.81e-5 m。
换算为毫米：2.81e-5 m = 0.0281 mm。
